title: Keep AC at 24 degC or higher
why: Air-conditioning is the largest end-use that can be estimated from campus data, and the rule of thumb is simple: each degree of setpoint raised saves energy.
typical_saving: About 6% of AC energy per 1 degC raised (24 degC instead of 20 degC is about 24%)
evidence_scope: General statement by BEE for room air-conditioners; not measured on this campus
needs: Current setpoints (a quick walk-through is enough)

title: Run AC only when the room is in use (timers or key-card switching)
where: The air-conditioned site with the most AC hours
why: Listed AC hours at the biggest site are long. Every hour of AC that runs in an empty room is waste, whatever the benchmark says.
typical_saving: Not a published percentage; the number shown is a formula (hours saved x units x power)
evidence_scope: Uses the listed operating days and hours, which are unverified
needs: Real hours of use per site (room booking or a simple log)

title: Match AC hours to working hours
where: The site with the second most AC hours
why: Same idea for the next largest site: office-type AC should follow office hours.
typical_saving: Not a published percentage; the number shown is a formula (hours saved x units x power)
evidence_scope: Uses the listed operating days and hours, which are unverified
needs: Real hours of use per site

title: Occupancy sensors for lights
where: Hostel washrooms, corridors, stairs and other common areas
why: Lights in common areas often stay on when nobody is there. A sensor switches them off by itself, the way malls do it.
typical_saving: On average about 24% of lighting energy
saving_source: Williams et al., LBNL-5095E (240 estimates from 88 studies)
evidence_scope: Mostly commercial buildings, not India; a hostel may differ
needs: Lighting load (fitting count x watt x hours) to turn the % into kWh

title: Replace old tubes and bulbs with LED
where: Wherever old fluorescent, CFL or incandescent fittings are still in use
why: Saving depends only on the old and new wattage of each fitting, so it can be worked out exactly once the fittings are counted.
typical_saving: Formula: (old watts - new watts) / old watts. No published average is used
evidence_scope: No campus fitting count exists yet
needs: Fitting count, old and new watt, daily hours

title: BLDC fans in classrooms, labs and hostel rooms
why: A BLDC fan draws far less power than an ordinary ceiling fan for the same air.
typical_saving: 28-32 W per BLDC fan against 70-75 W for an ordinary fan, about 54% to 63% less power per fan
evidence_scope: Manufacturer and programme figures, not measured on this campus

title: Check water pumps: run time and efficiency
why: Pumps that run longer than needed, or run at poor efficiency, waste energy quietly. Timers, level controls or a better pump can cut it.
typical_saving: About 20% of pumping energy through equipment and control changes
evidence_scope: Weak source: a general statement in an article, not a study
needs: Pump rating (kW) and daily running hours

title: Add more rooftop solar
where: Rooftop and shed areas not yet used
why: The campus already has rooftop solar, and its yield is measured, so the existing system is the best guide to what more panels would give. Wind is not suitable here.
typical_saving: The Optimization page models solar in blocks; the measured yield of the existing system should be used, not a general figure
evidence_scope: Needs the installed kWp of the existing system and the free roof area
needs: Installed kWp of the existing system and free roof area

title: Solar water heater, if hot water comes from electric geysers
why: Only useful if hot water is made with electricity today. If the hostel uses another fuel, skip this.
typical_saving: About 1,500 kWh of electricity a year for each 100 litres per day of hot water, when it replaces an electric geyser
saving_source: HAREDA (Haryana), Solar Water Heating System page
evidence_scope: Residential figure for Haryana, not measured here
needs: Whether hostels use electric geysers and the litres of hot water per day

title: Solar with battery backup instead of running the diesel generator
where: Buildings that depend on the generator during power cuts
why: Diesel is a small share of campus emissions, so this is not the first priority. Where the generator is needed only to bridge short power cuts, solar with a battery can do that job without diesel.
typical_saving: A CSE study of five housing societies found solar with battery backup costs about half as much per unit as power from a diesel generator (cost, not emissions)
saving_source: Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) policy paper, reported by Dialogue Earth
evidence_scope: Housing societies, not a college campus; cost comparison only
needs: Generator rating, how many hours it runs and why (power cut or test), battery and roof options

title: Electric buses for the college bus fleet
where: Diesel buses owned by the college
why: Buses are the larger diesel source. Electric buses use about 70% less energy per km than diesel buses, and the emission gain depends on how clean the grid is.
typical_saving: 19% lower use-phase emissions than diesel with the current grid, 34% in a cleaner-grid scenario, 96% with a fully renewable grid
saving_source: ICCT, Emissions reduction and benefits of the first 3,825 electric buses under PM-eBus Sewa
evidence_scope: City buses in India, use-phase emissions only; a college fleet with short routes may differ
needs: Daily km and route length per bus, charging point, price quote

title: Cut unnecessary generator running
why: Diesel is a small share of campus emissions, so this is a low priority. Still, testing and idle running can be reduced. There is no benchmark for generators, so this is a what-if, not a waste claim.
typical_saving: No published percentage; use the what-if on the Simulation page
needs: Reason for each run (outage or test) from the generator log

title: Switch-off routine: lights, fans and AC off in empty rooms
where: Classrooms, labs, offices and hostels after hours
why: No equipment needed. A simple end-of-day walk-through catches the waste that no meter can see.
needs: Nothing; start with a weekly checklist

title: Put meters on the main feeders
where: The Institute Building and the hostels
why: Most campus electricity has no end-use split today. Meters turn every guess on this page into a measured number, so this comes first for any real saving claim.
typical_saving: No saving claimed; it makes the others measurable
